key_insight: The paper introduces a scalable machine-learning interatomic potential that separates long-range electrostatics from local learned responses, enabling accurate energies, forces, and electrical properties at million-atom scale.
engineering_relevance: This makes device-relevant atomistic modeling under electric fields practical on distributed GPUs, bridging first-principles accuracy and large-scale simulation throughput.
method: Analytically split long-range electrostatic forces and Born effective charges into a global electrostatics solve plus local derivatives of learned latent charges.
Embed the formulation in an equivariant MLIP (DPA4C-LR) to preserve spatial decomposability for distributed evaluation.
Support energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across boundary conditions with scalable parallel computation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports scaling to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at about twice the cost of the short-range model, while reproducing BECs, field-dependent infrared spectra of water, relaxor polarization hysteresis, ionic conductivity, and Si/diamond interfacial thermal transport.
watch_item: The approach still depends on the quality of the learned latent charges and the electrostatics formulation, so transferability and boundary-condition handling need careful validation for new chemistries and geometries.
paper_title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
